title: Fibrewise dense opens of smooth schemes survive base change
statement: Let $f:Y\to T$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For $t\in T$, let $Y_t=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $V_t=V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose $V_t$ is topologically dense in $Y_t$ for every $t$. For every morphism $g:T'\to T$ of schemes, the open $V'=V\times_TT'$ is dense in each fibre of $Y'=Y\times_TT'\to T'$. Moreover, if $j':V'\hookrightarrow Y'$ is its inclusion, the map of sheaves $\mathcal O_{Y'}\to j'_*\mathcal O_{V'}$ is injective (scheme-theoretic density). The assertions allow empty fibres and arbitrary $T'$; no irreducibility of the fibres is assumed.

source.place: BLR 2.5, preliminaries on S-density and Lemma 1(b), printed pp.55-56 (PDF pp.61-62), applied also after base change; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $t\prime\in T\prime$ with image $t\in T$. By the fibre-product universal property, $Y\prime_{t\prime}\simeq Y_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t\prime)$, and similarly for $V$. The projection $q:Y\prime_{t\prime}\to Y_t$ is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open], applied with the field extension as the first factor. If $O$ is a nonempty open in $Y\prime_{t\prime}$, $q(O)$ is nonempty and open, so meets the dense open $V_t$. Consequently $O$ meets $q^{-1}(V_t)=V\prime_{t\prime}$. Thus every changed fibre has dense open, without an irreducibility hypothesis. The empty-fibre case is vacuous. The changed inclusion is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change].

It remains to prove schematic density for a smooth family with a fibrewise dense open; this argument will then apply to $(Y\prime,V\prime,T\prime)$. Indeed [lem-pc-smooth-flat] supplies flatness and local finite presentation of $f$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] at every point of $Y\prime$. Every image point is smooth, so $Y\prime\to T\prime$ is smooth locally everywhere and hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source].

Work on affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ chosen from the local finite-presentation charts of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; they form a basis after shrinking about a point. Restriction is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], $B$ is a flat finitely presented $A$-algebra. Intersecting a dense open of each fibre with this open chart is dense in that chart fibre. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-fibre-dense-quasi-compact-selection] to get a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq V\cap\operatorname{Spec}B$ dense in every chart fibre. Cover $W$ by principal opens contained in it and take a finite subcover: write $W=\bigcup_{i=1}^mD(b_i)$. This uses precisely quasi-compactness, not quasi-compactness of $V$.

source.place: BLR 2.5 Lemma 3, printed pp.56-57; finite principal refinement on an affine scheme

proof.text: Put $M=\prod_{i=1}^m B_{b_i}$ and let $u:B\to M$ be the tuple of restriction homomorphisms. Each $B_{b_i}$ is flat over $A$ by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness], since $B$ is $A$-flat. Hence $M$ is $A$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules]. For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, put $B(\mathfrak p)=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The fibre of the smooth chart is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. The open $W_{\mathfrak p}=\bigcup_iD(\bar b_i)$ is quasi-compact, with dense image. Its inclusion is quasi-separated since the diagonal of an open immersion is an isomorphism. Thus [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] identifies its scheme-theoretic image with the entire fibre, and [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] gives injectivity of restriction to $W_{\mathfrak p}$. The sheaf axiom on the finite cover by $D(\bar b_i)$ makes the map from its sections to the product of the principal-open section rings injective. Therefore $B(\mathfrak p)\to\prod_i B(\mathfrak p)_{\bar b_i}$ is injective.

The preceding map is $u\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Indeed finite products of modules equal finite direct sums, and tensoring distributes over a finite direct sum by the maps $(x_i)_i\otimes c\mapsto(x_i\otimes c)_i$ and their inverse given by summing the inclusions. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], $B_{b_i}\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\simeq(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))_{\bar b_i}$, carrying $(b/b_i^n)\otimes c$ to $(b\otimes c)/\bar b_i^n$. Thus the restriction tuple agrees on every pure tensor, hence on every element. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-finitely-presented-module-fibre-injectivity] with $\Sigma=\{1\}$ and $N=B$, free of rank one over itself. Its finite-presentation and both $A$-flatness hypotheses were verified above. Taking $Q=A$ gives injectivity of $u$.

If a section on this affine chart restricts to zero on $V$, it restricts to zero on every $D(b_i)\subseteq W\subseteq V$, so its image under the injective tuple $u$ is zero. The section is therefore zero. For any open $H\subseteq Y$ and a section vanishing on $H\cap V$, restrict it to the affine chart basis inside $H$ just used; each restriction is zero, and the sheaf axiom implies the original section is zero. This is the required injectivity of $\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_V$. Apply this conclusion to the changed smooth family from step 2 and its fibrewise dense open from step 1. If a chart or fibre is empty its section ring is zero; the empty product case forces $B=0$ by the same fibre criterion and causes no exception.

Source checks: the new node lem-sfb-smooth-fibre-dense-quasi-compact-selection is BLR §2.5 Lemma 3 exactly (read in the primary scan, printed p.56: X smooth and qc over S, U S-dense, so U contains a qc S-dense open). The new node lem-sfb-flat-finitely-presented-module-fibre-injectivity matches Stacks 0AT9 lemma-universally-injective-if-flat with its equation-star situation, hypothesis by hypothesis. Neither new node restates a clause of the item, and neither has proof or proof_deps. Duplicate checks: the 05DH, 05IA and 05IG universal-injectivity nodes are different statements, and the DAG has no Lemma-3 analogue. Steps: (1) the open projection Spec κ(t')×_{κ(t)} Y_t → Y_t, via lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open, gives density of the changed fibres. (2) The pointwise flat-smooth base-change node shows Y'→T' is smooth; the DAG has no scheme-level smooth base-change leaf. (3) lfp affine charts form a basis; Lemma 3 applied to Spec B gives W = ⋃D(b_i). (4) Smooth fibres are reduced; the Nagata reduced-dense-image and scheme-image-injectivity nodes, with W_p qcqs, give B(p) ↪ ∏B(p)_{b̄_i}; each B_{b_i} and their finite product are A-flat. (5) The localization-tensor identification plus 0AT9 with Σ={1}, N=B and Q=A gives B ↪ ∏B_{b_i}. (6) The sheaf axiom on the chart basis, applied to (Y',V',T'). Edge cases: m=0, an empty fibre, the nonreduced T'=k[ε], a non-qc V. Batch-5: the closure of lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change reaches lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion and two related trf smoothness lemmas. These are generic commutative algebra on smoothness, not steps of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs, so the flag is accepted.
